summary: Iter-29 verified the full-site crawl importer. Backend pytest: 16/16 pass in ~20s (test_iter29_full_crawl.py, xdist-parallel). Read-only assertions on the pre-existing 'Crawl Final' tenant (app_7035dfbf4a95, 5 pages of roto-rooter.com): premium_site_v==3 (blocks the startup premium-redesign migration), imported_from=='https://www.roto-rooter.com', theme.primary=#da291c / secondary=#2a1768 (both 6-digit hex from the site's real palette), brand_profile.phone='800-768-6911'. All 5 pages start with a shared navbar block and end with a footer block; footer columns[].links are strings (never objects — the previous canvas crash source); nav link signatures are identical across pages. No block prop in STRING_PROPS (cta/cta2/title/subtitle/heading/brand/badge/submit_label/email/phone/address) is a dict. NO external http(s) image URLs remain in any page block; only /api/public/files/... paths, and at least one is a real .png/.jpg. Media library GET /files lists imported files with uploaded_by=='website import', private=False; public GET /api/public/files/{storage_path} returns 200 with image/* content-type. Form block on /contact-us has valid fields[] (name/label/type/placeholder/required with types in the allowed set text|email|tel|number|url|date|textarea|select|checkbox|radio); posted a lead via POST /api/public/contact/{preview_token} and the marker appeared in GET /api/apps/{id}/inbox within 1s. max_pages clamp: max_pages=1 → exactly 1 page imported on example.com (~10s crawl); max_pages=0 clamps to min 1 and does not crash. Negative paths: invalid URL and http://localhost:3000 return friendly 400s inline; https://nonexistent-xyz-iter29.invalid errors gracefully inside the job. Viewer-role member gets 403 on import-preview / import / import-apply. Own-file upload: POST /apps/{id}/files with a 1x1 PNG succeeds and appears in the library; POST with a tiny mp4 is also accepted (used by the WebImport dialog's 'Add your own images, videos or documents'). Frontend Playwright smoke on /p/pv_d952e5d30466 (Crawl Final public preview, 1400x900): NO 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay; Roto-Rooter navbar renders with 5 top-level items + real dropdown children (hovering 'Plumbing' opens Emergency Plumbing / Water Heaters / Leaks / Garbage Disposals / Toilets / Showers & Bathtubs / Sinks / Faucets / Dishwashers / Washing Machines / Sump Pumps / Excavation / Septic Tanks / Pipes — 36 nav-dropdown elements). Home renders 'Call 800-768-6911' + 'Schedule Service' CTAs, TRUSTED SINCE 1935 badge, real hero copy, OUR SERVICES section with Emergency Plumber / Water Damage / Drain Cleaning / Water Heaters. On the /contact-us page (opened via the tenant page-bar tab in preview) form-block / custom-form / form-field-name / form-field-email / form-field-phone / form-field-message all render. Screenshots: iter29_preview_home.png, iter29_nav_hover.png, iter29_contact_page.png, iter29_form_filled.png.

issues: Second hero CTA button on some viewports renders as a bare white pill because cta2 is scraped as an empty string on a few pages — visible on 1400x3000 screenshot of home preview. Consider hiding the cta2 button when the label is empty.

action_items: Optional cosmetic: in BlockPreview.jsx hero/CTA renderer, skip rendering the cta2 button when the label is falsy/empty (currently an empty pill can appear next to the real CTA).
critical_code_review_comments: web_import._run_job: same fire-and-forget say() pattern from iter-28 is still present. 'applying' stage still races with a delayed 'rebuilding' write (rebuilding is fired via asyncio.create_task in build_import). Suggested fix: change `on` to an awaited coroutine (`async def say`, then `await on(...)` from build_import/crawl_site/save_images) OR drain pending stage tasks before writing 'applying'. Non-blocking for iter-29 assertions but keeps the UI 'Applying pages' step invisible on fast sites.

web_import.apply_import mode=='replace' still calls db.pages.delete_many({'app_id': app_id}) with no undo/backup. If a user runs a bad re-import, prior tenant pages are gone. Consider archiving to db.pages_history before the delete, or a soft-delete flag.

web_import._parse_forms: browsers/renderers may hide fields with CSS but here we accept anything not type in {hidden,submit,button,image,reset}. Fine, but the 20-fields-per-form cap and the search-form heuristic (skip single-field q/s/search) are conservative — a legitimate one-field newsletter signup ('email') will be preserved (name doesn't match), which is correct.

web_import.save_images: content-type sniffing accepts application/octet-stream if the URL extension is jpg/png/etc — good. But `if len(data) < 900: continue` silently drops small icons/logos and adds NOTHING to failures[], so a user won't understand why their favicon-sized logo wasn't imported. Add a failure entry ('image too small — likely icon/tracking pixel').

web_import.build_import: the global identity prompt is a single LLM call — if the LLM returns a footer with `links` containing objects rather than strings, the local flattening at line 526 handles it. Good defensive coding, matches the sanitisation goal.
web_import.OneShotIn / ApplyIn: no rate limit on how often the same tenant can trigger imports; a runaway client could spam LLM credits. Consider throttling to 1 running import job per tenant.

success_rate.frontend: 95% — canvas + navbar + dropdowns + form rendering verified visually and via selectors; form submit via UI was flaky due to page-bar tab click timing but backend equivalent (POST /public/contact/{token} → GET /inbox) passes cleanly
